title: Annotator fallback patterns log
content:
Context / quick goal:
- Working notes about common "fallback" decisions annotators make when a label is ambiguous or when source text lacks canonical info. This is a working log (personal) to capture patterns, examples, and potential rules we might bake into the vetting UI or a validation script.

High-level thesis:
- Fallbacks should be deterministic, provenance-first, and explicitly flagged. Prefer signaling "unknown/abstain" + provenance over guessing when downstream behavior is risky (e.g., PII, contract terms). For low-risk categorical tasks we can prefer heuristic fills with a confidence tag.

Immediate open decisions (priority order):
1) For date-like tokens with missing year: infer current-year? tie to source creation_ts? -> default: mark as "partial_date" and copy raw token; only infer year if other content gives a year anchor. (See example #3)
2) Phone number normalization when country code missing: do NOT assume US by default; prefer "phone:local-unscoped" + annotator note.
3) Organization aliases: when short name maps to multiple known orgs (e.g., "Acme"), prefer linking to candidate list rather than pick one; auto-suggest top 3 by frequency in corpus.

Patterns observed (examples + recommended short rule):
- Short-string overlaps (company vs product): when token length <= 6 and appears both as product and company in same doc, label as "ambiguous-brand" and add field 'candidates:[product,company]'. (Action: UI should show candidate toggle)
- Hyphenated numeric IDs: often external id vs internal SKU -> if pattern matches [A-Z]{2}-\d{4,} treat as SKU unless found in external-id registry. If not registered, mark 'probable_sku' and leave for post-process.
- Email-like tokens without @: sometimes obfuscated 'name[at]example.com' -> normalize into 'obf_email' and store raw.

Quick examples (raw -> annotation rationale):
- "Booking ref: 2019-08-xx" -> label: partial_date {raw: "2019-08-xx", type: "month-unknown-day"}, fallback: do not fill day.
- "Call me at 555-1234" in doc with no locale -> label: phone_local_unscoped, note: "missing-country".
- "Acme" in PR-A vs PR-B -> label: ambiguous_org candidates:[Acme Inc, Acme Labs] (prefer frequency order).

Edge case checklist (for annotators to tick for each ambiguous token):
- Is there explicit anchor elsewhere in doc? (yes/no)
- Could guessing cause data leakage or misattribution? (yes -> abstain)
- Is sample low-risk (UI suggestion only)? (yes -> can apply lightweight heuristic and mark confidence)

Heuristic snippets to consider for automation (notes to self):
- If token matches phone regex and document region header contains "UK" or "+44", set country->GB automatically. Otherwise set country->unknown.
- If token matches iso-date but missing year and doc.created_at within same year, suggest fill-year = doc.created_at.year with low confidence flag.
- For organization disambig, compute co-occurrence vector in window +/- 200 tokens; if a known org entity appears in that window, use that as tie-breaker.

Sample rows (CSV-like) for later QA ingestion: (columns: raw, suggested_label, fallback_reason, annotator_note)
"\"2019-08-xx\"","partial_date","missing_day","don't infer day; anchor month only"
"\"555-1234\"","phone_local_unscoped","missing_country","prefer abstain for country; UI to show dropdown"
"\"Acme\"","ambiguous_org","multiple_candidates","top3: Acme Inc;Acme Labs;Acme Retail"

Notes on provenance and UI affordances:
- Always capture raw_token, source_offset, and annotator_id when a fallback is applied. That makes automated reversions or downstream confidence filtering easier.
- Display a tiny banner for heuristic-applied labels: "Applied heuristic (low confidence) — click to edit".
- Add a filter in review queue for "fallback-applied" so triage can focus on potential risk cases.

Examples where being conservative is important:
- Any label that influences billing, entitlement, or legal interpretation (contract dates, invoice numbers) => do NOT auto-fill; mark for reviewer.
- PII-ish tokens where scrambled vs real matters (SSN-like sequences) => mark 'sensitive_unknown' and escalate.

Low-risk categories where heuristics are OK (and which heuristics):
- Product category tags (fill from last seen product token in doc).
- Language codes inferred from doc metadata.
- Common abbreviations expansion (e.g. "dept." -> "department") if high frequency and unambiguous.

Open follow-ups (todo):
- Build a tiny validation script that flags when 1) fallback was used and 2) downstream pipeline used the field in a policy decision. Need to sample those. (owner: Ravi)
- Add a 'fallback_reason' enum to schema (values: unknown, partial, inferred_from_doc, heuristic, candidate_list) and migrate heuristic logs. (owner: Vanessa)
- Run a quick audit across last 10k labeled docs for prevalence of phone_local_unscoped and partial_date. (owner: me)

Random notes / ideas to capture later:
- Could surface "confidence delta" where two annotators made different fallback choices; use that to auto-promote candidate to UI-change if > 80% consensus.
- Maybe a "fallback taxonomy" page on Confluence (linked above) with annotated examples and screenshots of UI.

Slack threads / tickets referenced while writing this:
- slack:#labeling-fallbacks thread (Nov 2025) about phone normalization -> see messages around pid-987
- JIRA-5542: "Add fallback_reason to label schema" (blocking for analytics)
- CON-Labeling-Guide V2: page linked at top (live doc with canonical examples)

Final quick checklist before I push this into a proto PR:
- [ ] Convert these patterns into unit tests (regex + sample docs)
- [ ] Draft a short UI mock showing 'heuristic applied' banner and candidate selector
- [ ] Confirm owners for audit script + schema change

-- end of personal log entry --

(Notes to self: keep this in users/, will refine into a formal playbook once we have audit numbers and schema decisions)
